Ukrainian grain at a crossroads: the strategic importance of the Lower Danube in wartime
snippet: War has changed the geography of Ukrainian trade, but it has not overturned its basic economics. For a grain exporter, what matters is not only whether cargo can leave the country, but also how much it will cost to deliver it to the buyer. On the Lower Danube, that calculation leads to some unexpected conclusions: a larger ship does not always mean cheaper transport, and a small change in shipment size can reverse one route’s advantage over another.
